# Child acquisition curves include VO and VOO {#sec-curves} ::: {.callout-important} ## AI-generated — not for publication The code and prose in this book were written by an AI agent under human direction; not line-by-line verified; must not be published or cited as-is. ::: ::: {.callout-warning} ## Preliminary & unvetted analysis Exploratory analyses of preliminary work; numbers not independently validated; check before use. ::: Schematic VL, VOL, VO, and VOO on 61 English CHILDES corpora from `tokens_filled.parquet` (childes-db 2026.1 gold parses plus Stanza-on-gloss fills). Remaining fully unparsed utterances are dropped. Each panel shows the eight most frequent child-produced verbs in that construction. Line-chart CDFs are inverse-weighted by total child tokens in each age bin so corpus coverage does not set the shape. Locative verb+preposition series are in the CSV tables. Model epoch curves are not scored yet. ::: {.callout-note} ## Filled parses Gold childes-db tags cover 14\,452\,928 tokens; Stanza-on-gloss added 175\,401 tokens. Extraction keeps utterances with POS and `%gra` so silver fills are included and leftover unparsed speech is not. ::: ::: {.callout-note} ## CDFs adjusted for sampling density Child tokens (any word) per 3-month bin range from 38\,529 (12 mo) to 737\,226 (30 mo); 5\,329\,842 child tokens between 12 and 72 months. Each verb's CDF uses verb-tokens / all-tokens in that bin, then renormalizes, so the shape tracks the word rather than how much CHILDES data happens to exist. ::: | Construction | Child tokens | |---|---| | VL | 51\,173 | | VOL | 31\,063 | | VO | 254\,606 | | VOO | 6\,049 | ::: {.callout-note} ## VO and VOO are verb-level Transitive VO and ditransitive VOO have no preposition grain. KM median first age: *want* 20 / *get* 21 months (VO). *give* 30 months (VOO; 281 producers). The 5-child earliest-median ranking on 962 children is dominated by rare lemmas, so the plots use token-frequency occupants instead. ::: ## Sampling-adjusted CDFs Each 3-month bin is weighted by this verb's tokens divided by all child tokens (any word) in that bin, then accumulated and renormalized to 100%. Lines are verbs produced by at least the construction-specific child minimum. Y-axis is cumulative weighted share (%). ::: {#cell-fig-cdf .cell fig-height='8' execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(10, 8), sharex=True, sharey=True) for ax, vac in zip(axes.ravel(), VACS): order = ORDER.loc[ORDER.vac.eq(vac)] keep = set(order.loc[order.n_children >= MIN_CHILDREN[vac], "verb"]) sub = CURVES.loc[CURVES.vac.eq(vac) & CURVES.verb.isin(keep)] verbs = order.loc[order.verb.isin(keep), "verb"] for verb in verbs: row = sub.loc[sub.verb.eq(verb)].sort_values("age_months") ax.plot(row.age_months, row.cumulative_share * 100, label=verb) ax.set_title(TITLES[vac]) ax.set_xlim(12, 69) ax.set_ylim(0, 100) ax.set_xticks([12, 24, 36, 48, 60]) ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="lower right", frameon=False, ncol=2) axes[0, 0].set_ylabel("Cumulative weighted share (%)") axes[1, 0].set_ylabel("Cumulative weighted share (%)") axes[1, 0].set_xlabel("Age (months)") axes[1, 1].set_xlabel("Age (months)") fig.tight_layout() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Sampling-adjusted cumulative token share by child age for the eight most frequent child-produced verbs in each schematic VAC.](01-acquisition-curves_files/figure-html/fig-cdf-output-1.png){#fig-cdf width=1186 height=947} ::: ::: ## First production by child, left-truncated and right-censored Each small dot is one child's first observed use of that verb+construction. Children enter the risk set at their first recorded child-speech session (left truncation). A first use in that first session is left-censored (acquired at or before first observation) and counted at entry. Children who never produced the combination are right-censored at their last parsed child-speech session and are not plotted as dots. The large marker is the Kaplan–Meier median age of acquisition; whiskers are a 95% bootstrap CI. If the KM curve never falls to 50%, the median is not reached and a dashed arrow shows the lower bound (if any). ::: {#cell-fig-km .cell fig-height='9' execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(10, 9), sharex=True) for ax, vac in zip(axes.ravel(), VACS): plot_km(ax, vac) axes[1, 0].set_xlabel("Age (months)") axes[1, 1].set_xlabel("Age (months)") fig.tight_layout() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![First observed production age (dots) with Kaplan–Meier median and 95% bootstrap CI (marker and whiskers). Verbs ordered by earliest KM median. Source: tokens_filled.parquet · 61 corpora · 962 children · childes-db 2026.1 + Stanza-on-gloss. Right-censored Kaplan–Meier with delayed entry.](01-acquisition-curves_files/figure-html/fig-km-output-1.png){#fig-km width=1186 height=1067} ::: ::: ## Kaplan–Meier median first age Same eight verbs as the plots above. Rank 1 = earliest KM median. Medians that are not reached (survival never falls to 50%) are listed last. The interval is a 95% bootstrap CI; a lower bound only means the median itself was not reached. Producers are children with an observed first use (`n_event`); never-producers are right-censored.
